title: FLORA CHAMBER SCARECROW CONTEST
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce Scarecrow Decorating Contest is now underway.

Registration is open to all businesses, organizations or individuals.  Scarecrows need to be on display near the front entry of your home or business no later than Sunday.  Judging will take place Monday, October 19th through the 26th.

Photos of all participating Scarecrows will be posted in an album on the Flora Chamber of Commerce Facebook page.  Like, comment or react to your favorites to vote.  If you don’t have Facebook stop by the Chamber office to cast your vote.

Voting will start on Monday with winners announced on October 27th.  Prizes will be awarded for people’s choice and Mayor’s choice.  For more information call Arriel at the Chamber office at 618-662-5646.

title: YOUTH HUNT
full_story:
Dan Hecht is having a free Youth Bird Hunt on Saturday November 7th.  The hunt is for those ages 10 – 16 wanting to experience Quail and Pheasant Hunting.  The location is the Hecht farm at 3362 Riffle Road near Iola, about 20 minutes South of Effingham.  The hunt times are from 9 am to 4 pm.

There will be Clay Pigeons for warm up, practice, and instruction.  There will be fields for first timers, as well as fields for the experienced hunters.

There will be a raffle to win a gun.  To help conservation efforts there will also be memberships for Quail Forever available.

Hunters should be sure to get a regular hunting License or an apprentice hunting license.  A gun safety course would be beneficial for Safety.

Please call the dealership and tell the receptionist that you want to attend the Youth Hunt in the morning or afternoon and how many will be attending.  The Phone number is 217-342-4111 or 217-821-4112 or email [email protected].

title: LOUISVILLE FALL HARVEST FESTIVAL
full_story:
The 75th Annual Louisville Fall Harvest Festival will start on Friday, October 30th.

Orders for Louisville Chamber of Commerce whole smoked pork loins can be purchased until October 25th, with pork loins to be picked up at Salt & Strings Butchery on November 10th from 4 to 7 pm.

The Kiddie Parade kicks things off at 2 pm, with Full Armor Christian School serving treats at the old Soda Fountain and the Red Brush Christian Church will be serving apple cider and the Louisville Christian Church will be serving free water near the pocket park.  From 4 to 6 pm the Methodist Church will be offering free chili with Das-zle Dance and tumble performing at 5:30 pm.  From 5:30 to 6:30 pm will be the past Queen reception at the State Bank Suite.  At 6:15 pm Sylvia and Meila Robey will sing on stage.  The Little Miss, JR Miss, and Queen pageants will be held at 7:00 pm.  There are 6 contestants vying for the title of Louisville Fall Festival Queen, The current Queen is Mila Zink.  There are 7 contestants in the JR Miss contest, the current JR Miss is Elsie Anderson, and there are 10 young ladies vying for the Little Miss title held by Landrey Eade.

The glow 5K walk, run will take place after the pageants.  Tomorrow is the last day to register for the walk, run, to guarantee a t-shirt, sign up at runsignup.com.  From 9 to 10 pm there will be music on the square with Seth Schnautz.

Saturday starts with the Rotary Pancake breakfast at 7 am, with tickets now on sale.  The FFA, AG Mechanics Tractor show will be on the east side of the square and kids activities will start at 8 am and the Clay County Genealogical Society Library will have an open house.  The Clay County Cruisers Car Show begins at 9, there will also be a greased pig contest, sponsored by the Hoosier Prairie Baptist Church, and a country store will open at the old Clay County Jail with free coffee and popcorn.

The Princess pageant will be on the main stage at 10 am with special guest Briley Mullins performing.  Starting at 11 am will be the Chili Cook Off Contest, hosted by the North Clay FCCLA and the Louisville Chamber of Commerce, with tastings available to 1 pm.  Contestants should bring their chili to the pocket park by 10:45 am.  Sign up by emailing [email protected], the winner will get a $50 prize.  At 11:30 Power and Grace Tumbling will perform on the main stage.  At 1 pm Deputy Trevin Smith and his K9 Chief will have a demonstration.  The parade is at 2 pm followed by the crowning of the Queens and the Rotary Basket Raffle winners will be announced.

For the Parade floats, cars, tractors, bands and Queens will line up at the grade school, horses will line up at the city park, Louisville Queens and contestants will line up on Magnolia Street, and Emergency Services will line up at the high school.  Handicap parking for the parade will be available on the east side of the square.

All weekend there will be arts, and crafts, food vendors, basket raffle and inflatables for the kids.

In conjunction with the Fall Harvest Festival Red Brush Christian Church will have a Trunk or Treat on Wednesday, October 28th from 6 to 7:30 pm, and the Louisville American Legion will have a meat shoot on Sunday, November 1st at 11 am.

title: BOARD MEMBER JAILED
full_story:
Wayne County Board District 4 member 45-year-old Steven K. Manning of Wayne City was jailed on firearm and wildlife violation charges.

Manning is facing preliminary charges of unlawful use of a weapon and a wildlife prohibited act.  Because he was arrested over the weekend and Monday was Columbus Day, his first court appearance will be today.   Department of Conservation Police made the arrest after an investigation regarding the alleged unlawful taking of deer.

Booking records show Manning was booked into the Wayne County jail at 10:05 pm Saturday.

title: SEMI’S COLLIDE
full_story:
Early Sunday morning Two semis collided on northbound I-57 at mile marker 133 between Kinmundy and Farina.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Department indicates that one truck broke down in the driving lane and was hit in the rear by the second semi, which didn’t see it in time to stop.  The impact caused the load of cat litter to be spilled onto the highway.

Both drivers escaped injury.  The cat litter was blown off the road before it reopened to traffic.

The crash occurred around 4:40 Sunday morning, and traffic was rerouted off I-57 onto Route 37 between Kinmundy and Farina for about a half hour while crews cleared the roadway.

title: WGH RECOGNIZED BY MODERN HEALTHCARE
full_story:
Wabash General Hospital District has been recognized by Modern Healthcare as one of the 2026 Best Places to Work in Healthcare, earning the Number 18 ranking among 75 organizations nationwide in the Provider/Insurer category.

The annual Best Places to Work in Healthcare program honors organizations that excel in creating positive workplace cultures, supporting employee engagement, and fostering environments where team members can thrive professionally while delivering exceptional patient care.

This marks Wabash General Hospital District’s seventh year being recognized on Modern Healthcare’s prestigious list, reflecting the organization’s continued commitment to its employees and the communities it serves.

“We are honored to be named one of Modern Healthcare’s Best Places to Work in Healthcare and especially proud to rank 18th among healthcare providers and insurers nationwide,” said Megan Prosise, Director of Human Resources.  “This recognition reflects the culture our employees create every day through their dedication, teamwork, and commitment to caring for one another and the communities we serve.  Being recognized on a national level reinforces what we already know; our people are the heart of Wabash General Hospital, delivering exceptional care close to home.”

With 682 employees, Wabash General Hospital District provides a comprehensive range of healthcare services throughout southeastern Illinois.  The organization continues to earn recognition for quality care, patient experience, and its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves.

The Best Places to Work in Healthcare rankings are based on an extensive assessment process that evaluates workplace policies, practices, demographics, and employee feedback.  For more information about Wabash General Hospital, go to www.wabashgeneral.com.

title: GATORADE RECALL
full_story:
More than 122,000 cases of Gatorade were recalled in 37 states, according to the US Food and Drug Administration.

The recall affects 28-ounce bottles of Gatorade Lemon Lime, Gatorade Lemon Lime Zero, Gatorade Orange and Gatorade Orange Zero, according to the FDA.  The products were recalled because they contain undeclared Yellow No. 5 and/or Yellow No. 6.

Affected Gatorade drinks were distributed to Alabama, Arkansas, Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Iowa, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, North Dakota, Nebraska, New Jersey, New Mexico, Nevada, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Washington and Wisconsin.

The recall received a Class II designation, which means the product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences, or that the probability of serious health consequences is remote.

title: FALL COVERS FOR SPRING SAVINGS
full_story:
Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA) is launching the eighth year of its Fall Covers for Spring Savings Program.

Participants can enter and validate their information during a pre-enrollment period starting at 8 am CST on November 30th.  Applications can be submitted once the program opens at 8 am on December 15th.  Entries may be saved and edited any time before submission.

A total of 190,000 acres are available for the 2026-2027 Fall Covers for Spring Savings program.  Funding of eligible acreage is on a first come, first serve basis.  Over the last seven years, the program has funded 890,000 acres of cover crops.

“The Fall Covers for Spring Savings cover crop premium discount program helps farmers lower their crop insurance costs while improving soil health, reducing erosion and enhancing long term land productivity,” said IDOA Director Jerry Costello II.  “It’s a practical way to strengthen both environmental stewardship and farm profitability at the same time.”

The program applies to Illinois acres seeded to cover crops in the fall of 2026 and planted to an insurable crop in 2027.  Eligible applicants will receive a discount of up to $5 per acre on their 2027 crop insurance premium, depending on individual crop insurance policies, for each verified cover crop acre.

Applicants must certify their cover crops with their local Farm Service Agency (FSA) office before applying and have their current FSA-578 and federal crop insurance policy number(s) ready.

The program encourages cover crop acres not supported by other state or federal incentives.  Please review the program rules page to check eligibility.  IDOA will use a combination of tools to verify that acres applied for through this program are planted in cover crops.  The program is only applicable for those with coverage through the United States Department of Agriculture Risk Management Agency (USDA-RMA) crop insurance program.  Approved applications will be forwarded to the USDA-RMA for processing and premium discounts on 2027 crop insurance invoices.

Pre-enrollment and applications are available at: apps.agr.illinois.gov/BLWR_CoverCrop/ or by following the program link on the IDOA website at agr.illinois.gov/.  Applications will be available until 11:59 pm CST on January 15th.
